name: extraction
description: Extraction in isolation: what survives the first stage, and in what wording. Assertions are deterministic — substrings, counts and regexes — so this runs in seconds with no judge model and no embeddings. It exists because two golden-set failures (a missed contradiction and a lost employer name) both turned out to be extraction problems, not decision problems.

cases.text: I work as a data analyst at Northwind Logistics. Been there two years.
cases.why: Dropping 'Logistics' made a later question about Northwind Logistics unanswerable.

cases.text: Our production cluster is called atlas-prod-7 and the staging one is atlas-stg-2. Don't mix them up.
cases.why: Identifiers are exactly what keyword retrieval is for — they have to survive verbatim.

cases.text: The on-call rotation for atlas-prod-7 is handled by the platform team, and alerts go to #plat-oncall.
cases.why: Handles and paths must not be paraphrased into prose.

cases.text: Keep the infra budget under $2,500 a month — that's a hard cap from finance.
cases.why: A number that gets rounded or dropped is worse than no memory at all.

cases.text: Had a peanut butter sandwich for lunch today and it was delicious.
cases.why: Trivial as an event, decisive as evidence about a stated allergy. Extraction cannot see existing memories, so it must keep what could bear on one and let reconciliation judge it.

cases.text: Ordered the ribeye last night, cooked perfectly.
cases.why: Same shape: an ordinary meal that contradicts a claimed diet if one is on file.

cases.text: I've been vegan for about three years now. Also, I really can't stand cilantro — it tastes like soap to me.
cases.why: Two unrelated facts in one sentence must not be collapsed into one memory.

cases.text: I like it when you keep answers short and skip the preamble.
cases.why: Memories are read back into prompts, so they are written about the user, not by them.
Reactions are not memories. Over-extraction is still a real failure mode.
Same — nothing here holds beyond this exchange.

cases.text: It's raining here again, third day in a row.
cases.why: Weather says nothing durable about the user; keeping it is noise in every future recall.

cases.text:
[1:56 pm on 8 May, 2023]
Caroline: I went to an LGBTQ support group yesterday and it was so powerful.
cases.why: A memory that says 'yesterday' is worthless a week later. When the text carries its own timestamp, relative references have to be resolved against it — this is the single reason every LoCoMo temporal question would otherwise fail.

cases.text:
[10:00 am on 3 March, 2024]
Sam: I'm flying to Lisbon tomorrow for the offsite.
cases.why: Same rule in the other direction, so it is a rule and not a memorised example.

cases.text: I went to the dentist yesterday and it was fine.
cases.why: With no timestamp in the text there is nothing to resolve against, and a guessed date is a false memory.

cases.text:
[1:56 pm on 8 May, 2023]
Caroline: Hey Mel! Good to see you! How have you been?
Melanie: Hey Caroline! I'm swamped with the kids & work. What's up with you?
Caroline: I went to a LGBTQ support group yesterday and it was so powerful.
Melanie: Wow, that's cool! Did you hear any inspiring stories?
Caroline: The transgender stories really got to me. I'm thinking about counseling as a career.
Melanie: You'd be great at that. I painted a lake sunrise last year that still makes me happy.
Caroline: I'd love to see it. I'm also taking the kids swimming next weekend.
cases.why: A whole session, not a single sentence. The one-line version of this test passed while a real LoCoMo session produced ten memories and not one date — the length and the competing topics are the failure, so the test has to carry them.

cases.text: Quick update: I moved from Berlin to Lisbon last month for a new job at Cobalt Labs.
cases.why: Relative time with no timestamp to resolve against. Asking for absolute dates made the model narrate its own uncertainty into the memory text — 'on a month before the messagessage was date, previisely unknown' — which is worse than the plain relative phrasing it replaced. A memory is a statement about the user, never commentary about the input.
